newsitem.title: FRANCE: Union seeks Jospin assurance on EMU flexibility.
newsitem.headline: Union seeks Jospin assurance on EMU flexibility.

text.p: The head of French trade union Force Ouvriere, Marc Blondel, said on Tuesday he wanted to meet Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to obtain confirmation the new government would push for a flexible interpretation of the Maastricht treaty on European Monetary Union.

Blondel told Reuters in a telephone interview that he sent a letter to Jospin on Tuesday seeking a meeting and reassurances on European policy before Jospin attends a European Union summit in Amsterdam on June 16-17 and a summit of the Group of Seven in Denver, Colorado on June 20-22.
"I sent a letter just after he took up his new functions this morning asking for a meeting to discuss what seem to me to be the most urgent questions," Blondel said.

"The most pressing problems are the upcoming G7 meeting and the (European Union) intergovernmental conference. This means that, in one way or another, policy will have to be reoriented, notably on economic convergence.

"Above all, I want him (Jospin) to spell things out in such a way as to leave himself a margin of manoeuvre, that precisely, he does not find himself in a position on the economic level where he has no room whatsoever to negotiate."

Blondel and other union leaders have been staking out positions on various economic and social issues ahead of the formation of a Socialist-led government, after an election on Sunday drove the centre-right government out of power.

"This means concretely, that especially concerning the three percent deficit (the goal for public deficits in the Maastricht treaty on EMU), that he has to try to get other countries to accept that it is a question of us moving towards the three percent, not an obligatory three percent," Blondel said.

"Because if it's three percent, and above all, if afterwards there is going to be a stability pact (on deficit control after the EMU launche) -- which I contest -- then this means he will be forced to produce another austerity plan, which I would contest under any terms."

Blondel's main obsession as one of France's high-profile union bosses has been defending the social security system and fighting the reforms instigated by the outgoing government under Alain Juppe in 1995.
